name: Citation Metadata
description: Core information used to identify, describe, and cite a dataset.

fields.name: Title
fields.definition: The main title of the Dataset
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Full title by which the Dataset is known.

fields.name: Subtitle
fields.definition: A secondary title that amplifies or states certain limitations on the main title
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
A secondary title used to amplify or state certain limitations on the main title.
Tip: The subtitle is not included in the auto-generated citation. If you want the subtitle to be included in the citation, then you must add itto the Title field in addition to the Subtitle field.the Subtitle field.

fields.name: Alternative Title
fields.definition: Either 1) a title commonly used to refer to the Dataset or 2) an abbreviation of the main title
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: A title by which the work is commonly referred, or an abbreviation of the title.Tip: Acronym, short form, or translation of full title.

fields.name: Alternative URL
fields.definition: Another URL where one can view or access the data in the Dataset, e.g. a project or personal webpage
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: A URL where the dataset can be viewed, such as a personal or project website.

fields.name: Other Identifier Agency
fields.definition: The name of the agency that generated the other identifier
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Name of agency which generated this identifier.
fields.example: Youth Communication Development Project, Education Department, Queen's University

fields.name: Other Identifier Identifier
fields.definition: Another identifier uniquely identifies the Dataset
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Another unique identifier that identifies this Dataset (e.g., producer's or another repository's number).

fields.name: Author Name
fields.definition: The name of the author, such as the person's name or the name of an organization
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: The author's Family Name, Given Name or the name of the organizatfion responsible for this Dataset.

fields.name: Author Affiliation
fields.definition: The name of the entity affiliated with the author, e.g. an organization's name
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
The organization with which the author is affiliated.
Tip: Use the full official name of the organization; avoid abbreviations.

fields.name: Author Identifier Type
fields.definition: The type of identifier that uniquely identifies the author (e.g. ORCID, ISNI)
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
Name of the identifier scheme (ORCID, ISNI).
Note: This field is a drop-down list; select one.

fields.name: Author Identifier
fields.definition: Uniquely identifies the author when paired with an identifier type
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Uniquely identifies an individual author or organization, according to various schemes.

fields.name: Point of Contact Name
fields.definition: The name of the point of contact, e.g. the person's name or the name of an organization
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: The contact's Family Name, Given Name or the name of the organization.

fields.name: Point of Contact Affiliation
fields.definition: The name of the entity affiliated with the point of contact, e.g. an organization's name
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
The organization with which the contact is affiliated.
Tip: use the full official name of the organization; avoid abbreviations.

fields.name: Point of Contact E-mail
fields.definition: The point of contact's email address
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: The e-mail address(es) of the contact(s) for the Dataset. This will not be displayed.

fields.name: Description Text
fields.definition: A summary describing the purpose, nature, and scope of the Dataset
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: A summary describing the purpose, nature, and scope of the Dataset.Tip: A good description will identify the content of the dataset and help a user determine if they have the technical ability to use it.
fields.example: The Social Media Use Among Teens survey was conducted by the Youth Communication Development Project to understand social media communication behaviours among youth in Canada. The survey collected responses from Canadian youth using an online questionnaire that asks about social media use including, platform type, frequency of use, activity type, and location of use. This information is supplemented with the respondent’s demographic and household characteristics

fields.name: Description Date
fields.definition: The date when the description was added to the Dataset. If the Dataset contains more than one description, e.g. the data producer supplied one description and the data repository supplied another, this date is used to distinguish between the descriptions
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: In cases where a Dataset contains more than one description (for example, one might be supplied by the data producer and another prepared by the data repository where the data are deposited), the date attribute is used to distinguish between the two descriptions. The date attribute follows the ISO convention of YYYY-MM-DD.

fields.name: Subject
fields.definition: The area of study relevant to the Dataset
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
Domain-specific Subject Categories that are topically relevant to the Dataset.
Note: This field is a drop-down list; select all that apply.Tip: Select one or more Subject terms to represent the broad domain or domains the dataset relates to.

fields.name: Keyword Term
fields.definition: A key term that describes important aspects of the Dataset
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
Key terms that describe important aspects of the Dataset. Can be used for building keyword indexes and for classification and retrieval purposes. A controlled vocabulary can be employed. The vocab attribute is provided for specification of the controlled vocabulary in use, such as LCSH, MeSH, or others. The vocabURI attribute specifies the location for the full controlled vocabulary.
Tip: The Keyword field is repeatable. Put each keyword in its own field by pressing the “+” button.Tip: In Dataverse metadata, keywords are case sensitive. Use sentence case for free text terms (i.e., capitalize the first word and proper nouns).
Tip: Use free-text terms or terms from a controlled vocabulary in this field to represent specific or granular topics associated with the dataset. Think of them like tags.
Tip: FASTand RVMFASTare  good, general-purpose controlled vocabularies adapted from Library of Congress Subject Headings (LCSH).Tip: Geographic place names should be entered in the Geospatial metadata section.

fields.name: Keyword Term URI
fields.definition: A URI that points to the web presence of the Keyword Term

fields.name: Keyword Controlled Vocabulary Name
fields.definition: The controlled vocabulary used for the keyword term (e.g. LCSH, MeSH)
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
For the specification of the keyword controlled vocabulary in use, such as LCSH, MeSH, or others.
Tip: Use this field when the Keyword term is from a controlled vocabulary
fields.example: Government of Canada Core Subject Thesaurus

fields.name: Keyword Controlled Vocabulary URL
fields.definition: The URL where one can access information about the term's controlled vocabulary
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
Keyword vocabulary URL points to the web presence that describes the keyword vocabulary, if appropriate. Enter an absolute URL where the keyword vocabulary web site is found, such as http://www.my.org.
Tip: Use this field when the Keyword term is from a controlled vocabulary.

fields.name: Topic Classification Term
fields.definition: A topic or subject term
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
Topic or Subject term that is relevant to this Dataset.
Tip: The Keyword field is repeatable. Put each keyword in its own field by pressing the “+” button.
Tip: In Dataversemetadata, keywords are case sensitive. Use sentence case for free text terms (i.e., capitalize the first word and proper nouns).
Tip: Use free-text terms or terms from a controlled vocabulary in this field to represent specific or granular topics associated with thedataset. Think of them like tags.
Tip: FASTand RVMFASTare good, general-purpose controlled vocabularies adapted from Library of Congress Subject Headings (LCSH).
Tip: Geographic place names should be entered in the Geospatial metadata section.

fields.name: Topic Classification Controlled Vocabulary Name
fields.definition: The controlled vocabulary used for the keyword term (e.g. LCSH, MeSH)
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
Provided for specification of the controlled vocabulary in use, e.g., LCSH, MeSH, etc.
Tip: Use this field when the Topic Classification term is from a controlled vocabulary
fields.example: Government of Canada Core Subject Thesaurus

fields.name: Topic Classification Controlled Vocabulary URL
fields.definition: The URL where one can access information about the term's controlled vocabulary
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
Specifies the URL location for the full controlled vocabulary.
Tip: Use this field when the Topic Classification term is from a controlled vocabulary.

fields.name: Related Publication Relation Type
fields.definition: The nature of the relationship between this Dataset and the related publication

fields.name: Related Publication Citation
fields.definition: The full bibliographic citation for the related publication
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: The full bibliographic citation for this related publication.
fields.example: Doe, Jane. (2017). Teen use of social media: analysis of self-reported communication behaviours. Journal of Social Media Use. Vol 1. Iss. 1, 2017.

fields.name: Related Publication Identifier Type
fields.definition: The type of identifier that uniquely identifies a related publication
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
The type of digital identifier used for this publication (e.g., Digital Object Identifier (DOI)).
Note: This field is a drop-down list; select one.
Tip: Use a persistentidentifier where possible (e.g.,DOI, handle, ISBN). If only a URL is available, select the type “url” and enter the URL into both the ID Number and URL fields.

fields.name: Related Publication Identifier
fields.definition: The identifier for a related publication
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
The identifier for the selected ID type.
Tip:If using ID Type “url”, enter the URL into both this field and the URL field.

fields.name: Related Publication URL
fields.definition: The URL form of the identifier entered in the Identifier field, e.g. the DOI URL if a DOI was entered in the Identifier field. Used to display what was entered in the ID Type and ID Number fields as a link. If what was entered in the Identifier field has no URL form, the URL of the publication webpage is used, e.g. a journal article webpage
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
Link to the publication web page (e.g., journal article page, archive record page, or other).
Tip: This field is only used for display purposes in the Dataverseinterface. For interoperability, ensure that the ID Type and ID Number fields are also completed.

fields.name: Notes
fields.definition: Additional information about the Dataset
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Additional important information about the Dataset.
fields.example: This survey was administered online. Mode of interview has been found to impact results,therefore it is not recommended that these results are compared with other survey results where the interview mode was telephone based.

fields.name: Language
fields.definition: A language that the Dataset's files is written in
values: Ho Chi Minh City Sign Language
Langue des signes de Belgique Francophone
Santa Ana de Tusi Pasco Quechua
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
Language of the Dataset.
Note: This field is a drop-down list; select all that apply.

fields.name: Producer Name
fields.definition: The name of the entity, e.g. the person's name or the name of an organization
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Producer name

fields.name: Producer Affiliation
fields.definition: The name of the entity affiliated with the producer, e.g. an organization's name
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: The organization with which the producer is affiliated.

fields.name: Producer Abbreviated Name
fields.definition: The producer's abbreviated name (e.g. IQSS, ICPSR)
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: The abbreviation by which the producer is commonly known. (ex. IQSS, ICPSR)

fields.name: Producer URL
fields.definition: The URL of the producer's website
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Producer URL points to the producer's web presence, if appropriate. Enter an absolute URL where the producer's web site is found, such as http://www.my.org.

fields.name: Producer Logo URL
fields.definition: The URL of the producer's logo
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: URL for the producer's logo, which points to this producer's web-accessible logo image. Enter an absolute URL where the producer's logo image is found, such as http://www.my.org/images/logo.gif.

fields.name: Production Date
fields.definition: The date when the data were produced (not distributed, published, or archived)
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
Date when the data collection or other materials were produced (not distributed, published or archived).
Tip: Date when dataset was finalized and ready for analysis or distribution.

fields.name: Production Location
fields.definition: The location where the data and any related materials were produced or collected
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
The location where the data collection and any other related materials were produced.
Tip: Include an institution if relevant. Avoid abbreviations.

fields.name: Contributor Type
fields.definition: Indicates the type of contribution made to the dataset
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: The type of contributor of theresource.Note: This field is a drop-down list; select one.

fields.name: Contributor Name
fields.definition: The name of the contributor, e.g. the person's name or the name of an organization
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: The Family Name, Given Name or organization name of the contributor

fields.name: Funding Information Agency
fields.definition: The agency that provided financial support for the Dataset
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Name of agency which generated this identifier.
fields.example: Youth Communication Development Project, Education Department, Queen's University

fields.name: Funding Information Identifier
fields.definition: The grant identifier or contract identifier of the agency that provided financial support for the Dataset
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: The grant or contract number of the project that sponsored the effort.

fields.name: Distributor Name
fields.definition: The name of the entity, e.g. the person's name or the name of an organization
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Distributor name.

fields.name: Distributor Affiliation
fields.definition: The name of the entity affiliated with the distributor, e.g. an organization's name
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: The organization with which the distributor contact is affiliated.

fields.name: Distributor Abbreviated Name
fields.definition: The distributor's abbreviated name (e.g. IQSS, ICPSR)
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: The abbreviation by which this distributor is commonly known (e.g., IQSS, ICPSR).

fields.name: Distributor URL
fields.definition: The URL of the distributor's webpage
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Distributor URL points to the distributor's web presence, if appropriate. Enter an absolute URL where the distributor's web site is found, such as http://www.my.org.

fields.name: Distributor Logo URL
fields.definition: The URL of the distributor's logo image, used to show the image on the Dataset's page
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: URL of the distributor's logo, which points to this distributor's web-accessible logo image. Enter an absolute URL where the distributor's logo image is found, such as http://www.my.org/images/logo.gif.

fields.name: Distribution Date
fields.definition: The date when the Dataset was made available for distribution/presentation
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
Date that the work was made available for distribution/presentation.
Tip: This field may be the same as the Deposit Date. Use Distribution Date only if data was previously distributed.

fields.name: Depositor
fields.definition: The entity, such as a person or organization, that deposited the Dataset in the repository
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
The person (Family Name, Given Name) or the name of the organization that deposited this Dataset to the repository.
Tip: The name of the person/institution who provided the dataset(s) to the archive (i.e., not necessarily the person preparing theDataverse repository submission

fields.name: Deposit Date
fields.definition: The date when the Dataset was deposited into the repository
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
Date that the Dataset was deposited into the repository.
Tip: Deposit Date is pre-populated with the date of upload to the Dataverse repository.  It can be edited to reflect the date when the data was received by an external or mediated data repository service.

fields.name: Time Period Start Date
fields.definition: The start date of the time period that the data refer to
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Start date which reflects the time period covered by the data, not the dates of coding or making documents machine-readable or the dates the data were collected.

fields.name: Time Period End Date
fields.definition: The end date of the time period that the data refer to
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: End date which reflects the time period covered by the data, not the dates of coding or making documents machine-readable or the dates the data were collected.

fields.name: Date of Collection Start Date
fields.definition: The date when the data collection started
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Date when the data collection started.

fields.name: Date of Collection End Date
fields.definition: The date when the data collection ended
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Date when the data collection ended.

fields.name: Data Type
fields.definition: The type of data included in the files (e.g. survey data, clinical data, or machine-readable text)
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Type of data included in the file: survey data, census/enumeration data, aggregate data, clinical data, event/transaction data, program source code, machine-readable text, administrative records data, experimental data, psychological test, textual data, coded textual, coded documents, time budget diaries, observation data/ratings, process-produced data, or other.

fields.name: Series Name
fields.definition: The name of the dataset series
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Name of the dataset series to which the Dataset belongs.

fields.name: Series Information
fields.definition: Can include 1) a history of the series and 2) a summary of features that apply to the series
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: History of the series and summary of those features that apply to the series as a whole.
fields.example: Established in 2005, the Youth Communication Development Project aims to gather key research and data about youth development and social media use through a series of independent, annual, cross-sectional surveys titled Social Media Use Among Teens. The overall objective of the program is to gather data on youth and social media trends in order to monitor changes in the well-being of young Canadians, and to provide information on specific social policy issues.

fields.name: Software Name
fields.definition: The name of software used to generate the Dataset
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
Name of software used to generate the Dataset.
Tip: Useful for specialized software or instruments.

fields.name: Software Version
fields.definition: The version of the software used to generate the Dataset, e.g. 4.11
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Version of the software used to generate the Dataset.

fields.name: Related Material
fields.definition: Information, such as a persistent ID or citation, about the material related to the Dataset, such as appendices or sampling information available outside of the Dataset
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
Any material related to this Dataset.
Tip: This is secondary materials in relation to the study description, such as technical documentation or a website detailing more information about the study.
fields.example: Youth Social Media Trends: 2015 Report [Canada]. YCDP, Queen's University, 2016. Access URL: http://dataverse.scholarsportal.info/queensu/2016report.pdf

fields.name: Related Dataset
fields.definition: Information, such as a persistent ID or citation, about a related dataset, such as previous research on the Dataset's subject
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
Any Datasets that are related to this Dataset, such as previous research on this subject.
Tip: This would include previous versions of the data (rounds or waves) or other collections generated by the same data.
fields.example: Social Media Use Among Teens, 2010 [Canada]. YCDP, Queen's University, 2011. DOI. Access URL: http://dataverse.scholarsportal.info/queensu/2010data.xhtml

fields.name: Other Reference
fields.definition: Information, such as a persistent ID or citation, about another type of resource that provides background or supporting material to the Dataset
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
Any references that would serve as background or supporting material to this Dataset.
Tip: This includes documentation such as codebooks, questionnaires, methodology, coding files, etc.
fields.example: Social Media Use Among Teens: Survey Questionnaire, 2015 [Canada]. YCDP, Queen's University, 2016. DOI. Access URL: http://dataverse.scholarsportal.info/queensu/2016questionnaire.pdf

fields.name: Data Source
fields.definition: Information, such as a persistent ID or citation, about sources of the Dataset (e.g. a book, article, serial, or machine-readable data file)
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: List of books, articles, serials, or machine-readable data files that served as the sources of the data collection.
fields.example: Statistics Canada. National Household Survey, 2011: Median Household Income by Census Tracts, Census Metropolitan Areas. NHS 2011, Statistics Canada. Access URL: https://www12.statcan.gc.ca/nhs-enm/2011/dp-pd/prof/index.cfm?Lang=E

fields.name: Origin of Historical Sources
fields.definition: For historical sources, the origin and any rules followed in establishing them as sources
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: For historical materials, information about the origin of the sources and the rules followed in establishing the sources should be specified.

fields.name: Characteristic of Sources
fields.definition: Characteristics not already noted elsewhere
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
Assessment of characteristics and source material.
Tip: Describes noteworthy aspects of the data collected.

fields.name: Documentation and Access to Sources
fields.definition: 1) Methods or procedures for accessing data sources and 2) any special permissions needed for access
fields.bestPracticeDefinition:
Level of documentation of the original sources.
Tip: May be used to explain any restrictions or access to source data documentation.

Macedonia, the Former Yugoslav Republic of
Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha

fields.bestPracticeDefinition: The country or nation that the Dataset is about.

fields.name: Geographic Coverage State / Province
fields.definition: The state or province that the Dataset is about. Use GeoNames for correct spelling and avoid abbreviations.
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: The state or province that the Dataset is about. Use GeoNames for correct spelling and avoid abbreviations.

fields.name: Geographic Coverage City
fields.definition: The name of the city that the Dataset is about. Use GeoNames for correct spelling and avoid abbreviations.
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: The name of the city that the Dataset is about. Use GeoNames for correct spelling and avoid abbreviations.

fields.name: Geographic Coverage Other
fields.definition: Other information on the geographic coverage of the data.
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Other information on the geographic coverage of the data.

fields.name: Geographic Unit
fields.definition: Lowest level of geographic aggregation covered by the Dataset, e.g., village, county, region.
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Lowest level of geographic aggregation covered by the Dataset, e.g., village, county, region.

fields.name: Geographic Bounding Box Westernmost (Left) Longitude
fields.definition: Westernmost coordinate delimiting the geographic extent of the Dataset. A valid range of values,  expressed in decimal degrees, is -180.0 <= West  Bounding Longitude Value <= 180.0.
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Westernmost coordinate delimiting the geographic extent of the Dataset. A valid range of values,  expressed in decimal degrees, is -180.0 <= West  Bounding Longitude Value <= 180.0.

fields.name: Geographic Bounding Box Easternmost (Right) Longitude
fields.definition: Easternmost coordinate delimiting the geographic extent of the Dataset. A valid range of values,  expressed in decimal degrees, is -180.0 <= East Bounding Longitude Value <= 180.0.
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Easternmost coordinate delimiting the geographic extent of the Dataset. A valid range of values,  expressed in decimal degrees, is -180.0 <= East Bounding Longitude Value <= 180.0.

fields.name: Geographic Bounding Box Northernmost (Top) Latitude
fields.definition: Northernmost coordinate delimiting the geographic extent of the Dataset. A valid range of values,  expressed in decimal degrees, is -90.0 <= North Bounding Latitude Value <= 90.0.
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Northernmost coordinate delimiting the geographic extent of the Dataset. A valid range of values,  expressed in decimal degrees, is -90.0 <= North Bounding Latitude Value <= 90.0.

fields.name: Geographic Bounding Box Southernmost (Bottom) Latitude
fields.definition: Southernmost coordinate delimiting the geographic extent of the Dataset. A valid range of values,  expressed in decimal degrees, is -90.0 <= South Bounding Latitude Value <= 90.0.
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Southernmost coordinate delimiting the geographic extent of the Dataset. A valid range of values,  expressed in decimal degrees, is -90.0 <= South Bounding Latitude Value <= 90.0.

fields.name: Reference System Information Reference System Code
fields.definition: An alphanumeric identifier for the reference system for the Dataset

fields.name: Reference System Information Reference System Code Space
fields.definition: The namespace of the system in which the reference system code is valid

fields.name: Spatial Resolution Value
fields.definition: The resource's spatial resolution, expressed as a value or as a brief textual description

fields.name: Spatial Resolution Type
fields.definition: Format in which the spatial resolution value is expressed

fields.name: Spatial Resolution Spatial Resolution Unit of Measure
fields.definition: If the spatial resolution value is expressed as a distance, the unit of measure that corresponds to that value

fields.definition: The type of geospatial data resource that is described in this Dataset record

fields.name: Resource Reference Date Date
fields.definition: A date which is used to help identify the resource

fields.name: Resource Reference Date Type
fields.definition: The type of date represented in the Date field
fields.example: revision, expiry, lastUpdate, lastRevision, nextUpdate, unavailable, inForce, adopted, deprecated, superseded, publication

fields.name: Data Lineage Statement
fields.definition: A statement about the Dataset's lineage

fields.name: Data Lineage Process Step Description
fields.definition: A description of the processes performed on the data as part of the Dataset's processing history

fields.name: Spatial Representation Type
fields.definition: The type of spatial representation of the data in the Dataset

fields.name: Vector Object Count

fields.name: Vector Object Type
fields.definition: Vector data only: The type of geometric objects (or shapes) that make up the structure of the vector Dataset
fields.example: curve, composite, complex, point, solid, or surface

fields.name: Raster Dimensions
fields.definition: Raster/grid data only: The number of independent spatio-temporal axes, or dimensions, represented in the Dataset

fields.name: Raster Dimension (Axis) Properties Raster Dimension (Axis) Name

fields.definition: Number of elements along the axis

fields.name: Raster Dimension (Axis) Properties Raster Dimension (Axis) Resolution
fields.definition: A decimal value representing a dimension's degree of detail, i.e. the size of the area that corresponds to a single data element along a Dataset's axis.

fields.definition: Resolution unit of measure for the dimension resolution value

fields.name: Raster Cell Geometry
fields.definition: Raster/grid data only: Identification of raster data in this Dataset

fields.name: Distribution Link Label
fields.definition: A descriptive label for the distribution link

fields.name: Distribution Link Protocol
fields.definition: The service or transfer protocol associated with the distribution link URL

name: Social Science and Humanities Metadata
description: Study design, data collection methodology, and population concepts used in social science and humanities research.

fields.name: Unit of Analysis
fields.definition: Basic unit of analysis or observation that this Dataset describes, such as individuals, families/households, groups, institutions/organizations, administrative units, and more. For information about the DDI's controlled vocabulary for this element, please refer to the DDI web page at http://www.ddialliance.org/controlled-vocabularies.
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Basic unit of analysis or observation that this Dataset describes, such as individuals, families/households, groups, institutions/organizations, administrative units, and more. For information about the DDI's controlled vocabulary for this element, please refer to the DDI web page at http://www.ddialliance.org/controlled-vocabularies

fields.name: Universe
fields.definition: Description of the population covered by the data in the file; the group of people or other elements that are the object of the study and to which the study results refer. Age, nationality, and residence commonly help to  delineate a given universe, but any number of other factors may be used, such as age limits, sex, marital status, race, ethnic group, nationality, income, veteran status, criminal convictions, and more. The universe may consist of elements other than persons, such as housing units, court cases, deaths, countries, and so on. In general, it should be possible to tell from the description of the universe whether a given individual or element is a member of the population under study. Also known as the universe of interest, population of interest, and target population.
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Description of the population covered by the data in the file; the group of people or other elements that are the object of the study and to which the study results refer. Age, nationality, and residence commonly help to delineate a given universe, but any number of other factors may be used, such as age limits, sex, marital status, race, ethnic group, nationality, income, veteran status, criminal convictions, and more. The universe may consist of elements other than persons, such as housing units, court cases, deaths, countries, and so on. In general, it should be possible to tell from the description of the universe whether a given individual or element is a member of the population under study. Also known as the universe of interest, population of interest, and target population.
fields.example:
• Canadians aged 12-30 (Source:https://doi.org/10.5683/SP/HY2H1A)
• Queen's University 2nd year medical students who were part of the 2016 Critical Enquiry Course in the School of Medicine and agreed to participate in the study.(Source:https://doi.org/10.5683/SP/D6NISS)

fields.name: Time Method
fields.definition: The time method or time dimension of the data collection, such as panel, cross-sectional, trend, time- series, or other.
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: The time method or time dimension of the data collection, such as panel, cross-sectional, trend, time-series, or other.

fields.name: Data Collector
fields.definition: Individual, agency or organization responsible for  administering the questionnaire or interview or compiling the data.
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Individual, agency or organization responsible for administering the questionnaire or interview or compiling the data.
fields.example: Trained student interviewers, both anglophone and francophone. (Source:https://hdl.handle.net/10864/ZJ17A)

fields.name: Collector Training
fields.definition: Type of training provided to the data collector
fields.bestPracticeDefinition: Type of training provided to the data collector
fields.example:
• The interviews were conducted by professional interviewers under the supervision of the Institute for Social Science Research. (Source: https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/SRVIO4)
